title: Taifa of Ceuta
capsule: The Taifa of Ceuta emerged from the fragmentation of the Hammudid emirate and the broader collapse of Cordoban authority in al-Andalus. By the 1060s the city and its hinterland were held by the Barghawata, a Berber group whose leader Saqqut commanded some 12,000 cavalry but practised a heterodox faith that alienated orthodox Muslim neighbours. The Almoravid Yusuf ibn Tashfin brought the taifa to an end in 1078–1079 when his forces conquered Ceuta, incorporating it into their expanding North African empire and using it as a springboard for the 1086 invasion of Iberia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Sources on this minor taifa are sparse; territorial extent is inferred from the city of Ceuta and its immediate surroundings, with no detailed boundary evidence surviving.
